column1: # The tropical forest, final list (Ronald, 11-04: "A + C's giants + some B"; Plants wires on tropical-trees). Canopy leaves in their OWN colours (fleaves), each with 3 random variants (_vN, cut to leaves_<x>/N.png).

# BLOCK_LIKE: w_* log_brazil_nut,log_brazil_nut_top,planks_brazil_nut,sapling_brazil_nut; l_* <worktree>/notes/blocks/tiles/study_bigleaf_1.png,leaves_brazil_nut; f_litter <study_leaf_litter_deep>; f_misc log_brazil_nut,heliconia

column3: log_andiroba|log|Andiroba bark: smooth grey-brown bark (#4a4038 #5e5248 #76685a #8e7f6e) with small flaking patches showing reddish under-bark (#8a4a36), few fissures
column4: log_andiroba_top|end|Andiroba log cut end: reddish-brown hardwood (#6a3426 #8a4632 #a65c42 #bc7456) with fine rings inside a thin grey-brown bark rim (#5e5248)
column5: planks_andiroba|built|Andiroba planks: reddish-brown hardwood planks (#5a2c20 #7a3e2c #964e38 #ae6448 #c27a5c), fine straight grain, four boards
column6: sapling_andiroba|plant|A young andiroba sapling: a thin grey-brown stem with two pinnate leaves of big glossy dark green leaflets (#1a3018 #24421f #32582a #46703a), about 18 px tall

column3: log_matamata|log|Matamata bark: smooth pale grey bark (#7a766e #928e84 #aaa59a #c0bbb0) with small dark lenticel dots and faint pale lichen patches, very few fissures
column4: log_matamata_top|end|Matamata log cut end: pale yellow-brown wood (#7a6648 #96805c #b09a72 #c6b088) with fine rings inside a thin pale grey bark rim (#928e84)
column5: planks_matamata|built|Matamata planks: pale yellow-brown wood planks (#6a583e #86704e #a08a64 #b8a27a #cab68e), straight grain, four boards
column6: sapling_matamata|plant|A young matamata sapling: a thin pale grey stem with several small leathery olive green leaves (#3a4420 #4e5a2a #667236 #808c46) and one bronze new leaf (#8a5a30), about 16 px tall

column3: log_ipe|log|Ipe bark: rough dark olive-brown bark (#3a3424 #4c4430 #605638 #766a46) in deep vertical fissures and ridges, very hard looking
column4: log_ipe_top|end|Ipe log cut end: dark olive-brown dense wood (#3e3420 #54482c #6a5c38 #807048) with very fine tight rings inside a rough dark bark rim (#3a3424)
column5: planks_ipe|built|Ipe planks: dark olive-brown hardwood planks (#36301e #4c4228 #625634 #786a42 #8c7c50), very fine dense grain, four boards
column6: sapling_ipe|plant|A young ipe sapling: a thin dark brown stem with two compound leaves of five light fresh green leaflets each (#3e6a24 #548a30 #6ea83e #8cc454), about 16 px tall

column3: leaves_andiroba|fleaves|Andiroba canopy leaves: only 4-5 big glossy DARK green leaflets 10-12 px long (#1a3018 #24421f #32582a #46703a #5e8a4a) with pale midribs and glossy highlights, overlapping at different angles, magenta gaps 20-30%
column4: leaves_andiroba_v1@-|fleaves|The same andiroba leaves, variant 2: the same colours and size, leaflets at different angles and places, magenta gaps 20-30%
column5: leaves_andiroba_v2@-|fleaves|The same andiroba leaves, variant 3: the same colours and size, different places, magenta gaps 20-30%
column6: leaves_andiroba_v3@-|fleaves|The same andiroba leaves, variant 4: the same colours and size, different places, magenta gaps 20-30%

column3: leaves_matamata|fleaves|Matamata canopy leaves: many small leathery OLIVE green leaves 6-8 px long (#3a4420 #4e5a2a #667236 #808c46 #96a058), a few bronze new leaves (#8a5a30 #a8703c), dense but with magenta gaps 20-30%
column4: leaves_matamata_v1@-|fleaves|The same matamata leaves, variant 2: the same colours and size, different places, bronze leaves elsewhere, magenta gaps 20-30%
column5: leaves_matamata_v2@-|fleaves|The same matamata leaves, variant 3: the same colours, no bronze leaves, different places, magenta gaps 20-30%
column6: leaves_matamata_v3@-|fleaves|The same matamata leaves, variant 4: the same colours, different places, magenta gaps 20-30%

column3: leaves_ipe|fleaves|Ipe canopy leaves: LIGHT fresh green compound leaves, palmate fans of five leaflets 6-9 px long (#3e6a24 #548a30 #6ea83e #8cc454 #a6d86c), bright and airy, magenta gaps 25-35%
column4: leaves_ipe_v1@-|fleaves|The same ipe leaves, variant 2: the same colours and fans, different places, magenta gaps 25-35%
column5: leaves_ipe_v2@-|fleaves|The same ipe leaves, variant 3: the same colours and fans, different places, magenta gaps 25-35%
column6: leaves_ipe_v3@-|fleaves|The same ipe leaves, variant 4: the same colours and fans, different places, magenta gaps 25-35%

column3: leaves_ipe_bloom|fleaves|An ipe crown in full bloom with no leaves: the whole square packed with clusters of golden yellow trumpet flowers 4-6 px long (#a07010 #c88a14 #e8b020 #f8d040 #fff08a), a few thin dark brown twigs (#4c4430) between, magenta gaps 15-25%
column4: leaves_ipe_bloom_v1@-|fleaves|The same ipe bloom, variant 2: the same golden trumpet clusters, different places, magenta gaps 15-25%
column5: leaves_ipe_bloom_v2@-|fleaves|The same ipe bloom, variant 3: the same golden trumpet clusters, different places, magenta gaps 15-25%
column6: leaves_ipe_bloom_v3@-|fleaves|The same ipe bloom, variant 4: the same golden trumpet clusters, different places, magenta gaps 15-25%

column3: leaf_litter_deep|cube|Deep rainforest leaf litter seen from above, like the attached study: a thick layer of fallen broad leaves 6-10 px long, brown, tan and dark red-brown (#3e2a1c #5a3e26 #7a5634 #9a7448 #b89462), a few green-gold fresher leaves (#8a8a3a #b0a040), fills the square, seamless
column4: leaf_litter_deep_v1@-|cube|The same deep leaf litter, variant 2: the same colours and leaf sizes, different leaves and places, seamless
column5: leaf_litter_deep_v2@-|cube|The same deep leaf litter, variant 3: the same colours, different places, one darker damp patch, seamless
column6: leaf_litter_deep_v3@-|cube|The same deep leaf litter, variant 4: the same colours, different places, a few more fresh green-gold leaves, seamless

column3: buttress_brazil_nut|log|The side of a buttress root fin of the Brazil nut tree: the same grey to grey-brown bark as the attached Brazil nut log (#4a4642 #5e5a54 #77716a #8e877e #a59d92), but its fissures sweep in long curves from the lower left and bend upward into vertical lines at the top, as if the bark flows up from the ground into the trunk; seamless left to right
column4: heliconia_green|plant|The same heliconia plant as attached but out of bloom: only the clump of big upright paddle leaves (#2e5a26 #427a32 #5e9a44 #7cb458) with pale midribs, no flower spike, about 22 px tall
